facts.statement: Triceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Triceratops lived approximately 69 to 66 million years ago during the late Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: lived during the late Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period, about 69 to 66 million years ago

facts.statement: Triceratops inhabited the island continent of Laramidia, which corresponds to modern-day western North America.
facts.quote: on the island continent of Laramidia, now forming western North America

facts.statement: Triceratops possessed a large bony frill, three skull horns, and a large quadrupedal body.
facts.quote: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body

facts.statement: Triceratops measured approximately 8 to 9 meters in length and weighed between 6 and 10 metric tons.
facts.quote: measuring around 8 - 9 m long and weighing up to 6 - 10 MT

facts.statement: The name Triceratops means 'three-horned face', derived from Ancient Greek words for three, horn, and face.
facts.quote: The name Triceratops, which means 'three-horned face', is derived from Ancient Greek trí- (), meaning 'three', kéras (), meaning 'horn', and ṓps (), meaning 'face'

facts.statement: Triceratops likely shared its environment with and was preyed upon by Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: It shared the landscape with and was most likely preyed upon by Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate regarding the function of Triceratops' frill and horns, with traditional views favoring defense against predators and recent interpretations suggesting roles in species identification, courtship, and dominance displays.
facts.quote: The functions of the frills and three distinctive facial horns on its head have inspired countless debates. Traditionally, these have been viewed as defensive weapons against predators. More recent interpretations find it probable that these features were primarily used in species identification, courtship, and dominance display

facts.statement: Triceratops is classified as a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Triceratops ( ; ) is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur

facts.statement: While traditionally classified among short-frilled ceratopsids, modern studies place Triceratops within Chasmosaurinae, a group typically characterized by long frills.
facts.quote: Triceratops was traditionally placed within the "short-frilled" ceratopsids, but modern cladistic studies show it to be a member of Chasmosaurinae, which usually have long frills

facts.statement: Currently, only two species of Triceratops are considered valid: T. horridus and T. prorsus.
facts.quote: Two species, T. horridus and T. prorsus, are considered valid today

facts.statement: The genus Triceratops was first described in 1889 by the American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
facts.quote: described in 1889 by American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh

facts.statement: The first fossil specimen attributed to Triceratops was found by George Lyman Cannon near Denver, Colorado, in the spring of 1887.
facts.quote: The first named fossil specimen now attributed to Triceratops is a pair of brow horns attached to a skull roof that were found by George Lyman Cannon near Denver, Colorado, in the spring of 1887

facts.statement: The Triceratops holotype (YPM 1820) was collected in 1888 from the Lance Formation of Wyoming by fossil hunter John Bell Hatcher.
facts.quote: The Triceratops holotype, YPM 1820, was collected in 1888 from the Lance Formation of Wyoming by fossil hunter John Bell Hatcher

facts.statement: The discovery of the holotype involved cowboy Edmund B. Wilson, who found a horn after a skull broke off during an attempt to lasso it, and subsequently showed it to his boss, Charles Arthur Guernsey, who informed Hatcher.
facts.quote: Cowboy Edmund B. Wilson had been startled by the sight of a monstrous skull poking out of the side of a ravine. He tried to recover it by throwing a lasso around one of the horns. When it broke off, the skull tumbling to the bottom of the cleft, Wilson brought the horn to his boss. His boss was rancher and avid fossil collector Charles Arthur Guernsey, who just so happened to show it to Hatcher

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh initially described the holotype specimen as a different species of Ceratops before renaming it Triceratops.
facts.quote: Marsh initially described this specimen as another species of Ceratops

facts.statement: Marsh renamed the specimen Triceratops after further preparation revealed a third nose horn.
facts.quote: When further preparation uncovered the third nose horn, Marsh changed his mind and gave the piece the new generic name Triceratops

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope described two taxa, Agathaumas sylvestris and Polyonax mortuarius, in 1872 and 1874, which may belong to Triceratops but are fragmentary.
facts.quote: fossils possibly belonging to Triceratops were described as two taxa, Agathaumas sylvestris and Polyonax mortuarius, in 1872 and 1874, respectively, by Marsh's archrival Edward Drinker Cope

facts.statement: Agathaumas was named based on remains collected by Fielding Bradford Meek and Henry Martyn Bannister near the Green River in southeastern Wyoming from the Maastrichtian Lance Formation.
facts.quote: Agathaumas was named based on a pelvis, several vertebrae, and a few ribs collected by Fielding Bradford Meek and Henry Martyn Bannister near the Green River of southeastern Wyoming from layers coming from the Maastrichtian Lance Formation

facts.statement: Polyonax mortuarius was collected by Edward Drinker Cope in 1873 from northeastern Colorado, possibly from the Maastrichtian Denver Formation.
facts.quote: Polyonax mortuarius was collected by Cope himself in 1873 from northeastern Colorado, possibly coming from the Maastrichtian Denver Formation

facts.statement: The fossils of Polyonax mortuarius consisted only of fragmentary horn cores, three dorsal vertebrae, and limb elements.
facts.quote: The fossils only consisted of fragmentary horn cores, 3 dorsal vertebrae, and fragmentary limb elements

facts.statement: Marsh initially described the holotype specimen as another species of Ceratops before renaming it Triceratops.
facts.quote: Marsh initially described this specimen as another species of Ceratops

facts.statement: Between 1889 and 1891, John Bell Hatcher collected thirty-one additional Triceratops skulls.
facts.quote: After Triceratops was described, between 1889 and 1891, Hatcher collected another thirty-one of its skulls with great effort

facts.statement: The specific name horridus for T. horridus is derived from the Latin word for 'rough' or 'rugose', possibly referring to the texture of an aged type specimen.
facts.quote: Its specific name was derived from the Latin word meaning "rough" or "rugose", perhaps referring to the type specimen's rough texture, later identified as an aged individual

facts.statement: In 1986, John Ostrom and Peter Wellnhofer proposed that all Triceratops remains belong to a single species, T. horridus.
facts.quote: In 1986, John Ostrom and Peter Wellnhofer published a paper in which they proposed that there was only one species, Triceratops horridus

facts.statement: Thomas Lehman suggested that different Triceratops lineages represented sexual dimorphism and maturity, including females, males, and pathologic old males.
facts.quote: Thomas Lehman added the old Lull–Sternberg lineages combined with maturity and sexual dimorphism, suggesting that the T. horridus–T. prorsus–T. brevicornus lineage was composed of females, the T. calicornis–T. elatus lineage was made up of males, and the T. obtusus–T. hatcheri lineage was of pathologic old males

facts.statement: In 2014, John Scannella and colleagues supported separating T. prorsus and T. horridus, noting they were separated stratigraphically within the Hell Creek Formation and likely did not coexist.
facts.quote: In 2014, John Scannella and colleagues supported the separation of T. prorsus and T. horridus, noting that the two species are also separated stratigraphically within the Hell Creek Formation, indicating that they did not live together at the same time

facts.statement: T. horridus is the type species of Triceratops, originally described as Ceratops by Marsh in 1889.
facts.quote: T. horridus (Marsh, 1889) Marsh, 1889 (originally Ceratops) (type species)

facts.statement: T. prorsus is a valid species of Triceratops described by Marsh in 1890.
facts.quote: T. prorsus Marsh, 1890

facts.statement: Triceratops was a massive animal, reaching lengths of 8 to 9 meters and weighing between 6 and 10 metric tons.
facts.quote: Triceratops was a very large animal, measuring around 8 - 9 m in length and weighing up to 6 - 10 MT.

facts.statement: A specific specimen named Kelsey measured 22 to 24 feet long, had a 6.5-foot skull, stood 7.5 feet tall, and weighed approximately 5.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: A specimen of T. horridus named Kelsey measured 22 - 24 ft long, has a 6.5 ft skull, stood about 7.5 ft tall, and was estimated by the Black Hills Institute to weigh approximately 5.4 MT.

facts.statement: A specimen named Big John was estimated to be 26.1 feet long and 10 feet tall.
facts.quote: A T. horridus specimen named Big John was estimated to have been 26.1 ft long and 10 ft tall.

facts.statement: The largest known skull, specimen MWC 7584, was estimated to be 2.5 meters long when complete, representing nearly one-third of the animal's total length.
facts.quote: The largest-known skull, specimen MWC 7584 (formerly BYU 12183), is estimated to have been 2.5 m in length when complete and could reach almost a third of the length of the entire animal.

facts.statement: Triceratops possessed a large beak at the front of its head, formed by a specialized rostral bone.
facts.quote: The front of the head was equipped with a large beak in front of its teeth. The core of the top beak was formed by a special rostral bone.

facts.statement: A single horn was located on the snout above the nostrils.
facts.quote: The skull bore a single horn on the snout above the nostrils.

facts.statement: Triceratops had a pair of brow horns approximately 1 meter long, positioned above each eye.
facts.quote: The skull also featured a pair of supraorbital "brow" horns approximately 1 m long, with one above each eye.

facts.statement: Unlike most relatives that had large openings in their frills, Triceratops had a noticeably solid frill, though this may vary if Torosaurus represents mature individuals.
facts.quote: Most other ceratopsids had large parietal fenestrae, openings in their frills, but those of Triceratops were noticeably solid, unless the genus Torosaurus represents mature Triceratops individuals, which it most likely does not.

facts.statement: A huge occipital condyle up to 106 millimeters in diameter connected the skull to the neck under the frill.
facts.quote: Under the frill, at the rear of the skull, a huge occipital condyle, up to 106 mm in diameter, connected the head to the neck.

facts.statement: Triceratops had a sturdy build with strong limbs, short hands ending in three hooves, and short feet ending in four hooves.
facts.quote: Both Triceratops species possessed a very sturdy build, with strong limbs, short hands with three hooves each, and short feet with four hooves each.

facts.statement: The vertebral column consisted of ten neck vertebrae, twelve back vertebrae, ten sacral vertebrae, and approximately forty-five tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column consisted of ten neck, twelve back, ten sacral, and about forty-five tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: The spinous processes of the neck in Triceratops were constant in height and did not gradually slope upwards.
facts.quote: In Triceratops, the spinous processes of the neck are constant in height and don't gradually slope upwards.

facts.statement: While Triceratops was certainly quadrupedal, there is debate regarding its posture, with some believing its front legs sprawled at a considerable angle to support the head's weight.
facts.quote: Although certainly quadrupedal, the posture of horned dinosaurs has long been the subject of some debate. Originally, it was believed that the front legs of the animal had to be sprawling at a considerable angle from the thorax in order to better bear the weight of the head.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of the hand is 2-3-4-3-1, indicating the number of bones in each finger from the innermost to the outermost.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula of the hand is 2-3-4-3-1, meaning that the first or innermost finger of the forelimb has two bones, the next has three, the next has four, etc.

facts.statement: The fossilized skin of specimen "Lane" was preserved via a unique process called "clay templating," where a bacterial mat formed a clay layer that recorded the skin in positive relief.
facts.quote: The skin is not preserved as an impression but as a thin layer of clay that formed from a bacterial mat on the desiccated body and recorded the skin in positive relief with exceptional detail, a form of fossilization called "clay templating"

facts.statement: The large basement scales covering most of the Triceratops body are the largest known in ceratopsians, reaching up to 9 cm across.
facts.quote: The basement scales covering the majority of the body are large in size, the largest known in ceratopsians at up to 9 cm across

facts.statement: Large feature scales scattered approximately 15-20 cm apart among the basement scales exceed 10 cm across and are hexagonal or heptagonal in shape.
facts.quote: Regularly scattered (approximately 15-20 cm from each other, though in no particular pattern) amongst the basement scales are large feature scales, exceeding 10 cm across, which are hexagonal (six-sided) to heptagonal (seven-sided) in shape

facts.statement: Researchers suggest it is unlikely that the nipple-like projections on Triceratops feature scales bore bristles, unlike those found in other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that it is unlikely that the nipple-like projections of the feature scales bore bristles like those known in other ceratopsians like Psittacosaurus

facts.statement: Thomas Lehman defined the subfamilies in 1990 and diagnosed Triceratops as a "ceratopsine" based on several morphological features.
facts.quote: Thomas Lehman defining both subfamilies in 1990 and diagnosing Triceratops as "ceratopsine" on the basis of several morphological features

facts.statement: Remains of a Triceratops group show signs of predation or scavenging by Tyrannosaurus, including breakage and puncture wounds on the front limbs of the largest specimen.
facts.quote: The remains also show signs of predation or scavenging from Tyrannosaurus, particularly on the largest specimen, with the bones of the front limbs showing breakage and puncture wounds from Tyrannosaurus teeth

facts.statement: A 2020 study described co-ossified tail vertebrae in Triceratops, suggesting the condition arose after one individual stepped on the tail of another.
facts.quote: In 2020, Illies and Fowler described the co-ossified distal caudal vertebrae of Triceratops. According to them, this pathology could have arisen after one Triceratops accidentally stepped on the tail of another member of the herd

facts.statement: A 2026 study suggests Triceratops had respiratory turbinates that cooled blood to the eyes and brain by evaporating moisture, preventing overheating in their large skulls.
facts.quote: A 2026 study of the large nasal region suggested that Triceratops likely had respiratory turbinates which contained moisture that evaporated as air was inhaled. This released heat and cooled the blood directed to the eyes and brain, which would otherwise overheat within their large, thick skulls

facts.statement: A 2022 study suggests Triceratops had an ectothermic or gigantothermic metabolism similar to modern reptiles.
facts.quote: A 2022 study by Wiemann and colleagues of various dinosaur genera, including Triceratops, suggests that it had an ectothermic (cold blooded) or gigantothermic metabolism, on par with that of modern reptiles

facts.statement: Triceratops lived in environments consisting of floodplains and inland forests.
facts.quote: The very same study conducted by Wiemann et al., revealed that Triceratops lived in environments that consisted of floodplains and inland forests

facts.statement: Triceratops were herbivores that primarily ate low-growing vegetation but could potentially knock down taller plants using their horns, beak, and bulk.
facts.quote: Triceratops were herbivorous and, because of their low-slung head, their primary food was probably low-growing vegetation, although they may have been able to knock down taller plants with their horns, beak, and sheer bulk.

facts.statement: Triceratops possessed between 432 and 800 teeth in total, with only a fraction in use at any time due to continuous replacement throughout their lives.
facts.quote: This gives a range of 432 to 800 teeth, of which only a fraction were in use at any given time (as tooth replacement was continuous throughout the life of the animal).

facts.statement: Triceratops consumed various plants including Populus, Pine, Platanus, Hazel, and Taxodium.
facts.quote: Other plants that were a part of its diet included Populus plants, Pine plants, Platanus plants, Hazel plants, and Taxodium plants.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Triceratops ate palms and cycads or ferns growing in prairies.
facts.quote: Some researchers suggest it, along with its cousin Torosaurus ate palms and cycads and others suggest it ate ferns, which then grew in prairies.

facts.statement: While combat and courtship display are the main theories for Triceratops head adornments, courtship display is now considered the most likely primary function.
facts.quote: There has been much speculation over the functions of Triceratops head adornments. The two main theories have revolved around use in combat and in courtship display, with the latter now thought to be the most likely primary function.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Peter Dodson estimates that a Triceratops could successfully defend itself against a bull Tyrannosaurus by inflicting fatal wounds with its sharp horns.
facts.quote: Paleontologist Peter Dodson estimates that, in a battle against a bull Tyrannosaurus, the Triceratops had the upper hand and would successfully defend itself by inflicting fatal wounds to the Tyrannosaurus using its sharp horns.

facts.statement: Tyrannosaurus is known to have consumed Triceratops, evidenced by a heavily tooth-scored Triceratops ilium and sacrum.
facts.quote: Tyrannosaurus is also known to have consumed Triceratops, as shown by a heavily tooth-scored Triceratops ilium and sacrum showing Tyrannosaurus feeding traces.

facts.statement: A 2006 study found no evidence that pitting, holes, and lesions on Triceratops skulls were caused by horn thrust injuries, suggesting other causes like bone disease.
facts.quote: Although pitting, holes, lesions, and other damage on Triceratops skulls (and the skulls of other ceratopsids) are often attributed to horn damage in combat, a 2006 study finds no evidence for horn thrust injuries causing these forms of damage (with there being no evidence of infection or healing).

facts.statement: A 2009 study suggests Triceratops used horns in combat and the frill as protection, whereas Centrosaurus may have used cranial ornamentation for visual display or body-focused combat.
facts.quote: A 2009 study compared incidence rates of skull lesions and periosteal reaction in Triceratops and Centrosaurus, showing that these were consistent with Triceratops using its horns in combat and the frill being adapted as a protective structure, while lower pathology rates in Centrosaurus may indicate visual use over physical use of cranial ornamentation or a form of combat focused on the body rather than the head.

facts.statement: Studies found that the frequency of injury in Triceratops was 14%.
facts.quote: The frequency of injury was found to be 14% in Triceratops.

facts.statement: A Triceratops skull was found with a healed puncture wound in the jugal bone, likely caused by another Triceratops horn.
facts.quote: One skull was found with a hole in the jugal bone, apparently a puncture wound sustained while the animal was alive, as indicated by signs of healing.

facts.statement: The specimen "Big John" shows a healed wound on the squamosal bone caused by another Triceratops horn, supporting the hypothesis of intra-specific combat.
facts.quote: Another specimen, referred to as "Big John", has a similar fenestra to the squamosal caused by what appears to be another Triceratops horn and the squamosal bone shows signs of significant healing, further vindicating the hypothesis that this ceratopsian used its horns for intra-specific combat.

facts.statement: The large frill of Triceratops may have helped regulate body temperature by increasing surface area.
facts.quote: The large frill also may have helped to increase body area to regulate body temperature.

facts.statement: The idea that Triceratops cranial structures were used for species recognition is debated because no modern species uses such structures for this purpose.
facts.quote: However, the use of the exaggerated structures to enable dinosaurs to recognize their own species has been questioned, as no such function exists for such structures in modern species.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists investigating fossils in Montana's Hell Creek Formation argue that Torosaurus and Triceratops represent a single genus.
facts.quote: Paleontologists investigating dinosaur ontogeny in Montana's Hell Creek Formation have presented evidence that the two represent a single genus

facts.statement: In a paper presented in September 2009, John Scannella reclassified Torosaurus as especially mature individuals of Triceratops.
facts.quote: John Scannella, in a paper presented in Bristol at the conference of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology (September 25, 2009), reclassified Torosaurus as especially mature Triceratops individuals

facts.statement: Torosaurus is distinguished by an elongated skull and two oval openings in its frill.
facts.quote: Its distinguishing features are an elongated skull and the presence of two ovular fenestrae in the frill

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the bone in ceratopsian skulls is metaplastic, allowing it to change shape over time.
facts.quote: A characteristic of metaplastic bone is that it lengthens and shortens over time, extending and resorbing to form new shapes

facts.statement: In 2006, Andrew Farke argued that no systematic differences exist between Torosaurus and Triceratops other than the frill.
facts.quote: Andrew Farke had, in 2006, stressed that no systematic differences could be found between Torosaurus and Triceratops, apart from the frill

facts.statement: Longrich and Field concluded that the fossil record contains both old Triceratops individuals and young Torosaurus individuals, challenging the idea that they are the same species.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that Triceratops individuals too old to be considered immature forms are represented in the fossil record, as are Torosaurus individuals too young to be considered fully mature adults

facts.statement: Research indicates that Torosaurus lived during the Late Maastrichtian, contemporaneously with Triceratops.
facts.quote: The same study also noted that Torosaurus indeed lived during the Late Maastrichtian (contemporaneously with Triceratops)

facts.statement: Scientific opinion has varied regarding whether Nedoceratops is a valid separate genus.
facts.quote: Opinion has varied on the validity of a separate genus for Nedoceratops

facts.statement: Longrich and Fields suggested that the frill holes in Nedoceratops were pathological rather than a transitional feature between Torosaurus and Triceratops.
facts.quote: Longrich and Fields also did not consider it a transition between Torosaurus and Triceratops, suggesting that the frill holes were pathological

facts.statement: Nicholas Longrich suggested that the genus Ojoceratops is a synonym of Triceratops.
facts.quote: Longrich agreed with Scannella about Nedoceratops and made a further suggestion that the recently described Ojoceratops was likewise a synonym

facts.statement: Longrich observed that the genus Tatankaceratops displayed a mix of adult and juvenile Triceratops characteristics.
facts.quote: Longrich observed that another newly described genus, Tatankaceratops, displayed a strange mix of characteristics already found in adult and juvenile Triceratops

facts.statement: Longrich suggested that Tatankaceratops could represent a dwarf Triceratops or an individual with a developmental disorder rather than a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Rather than representing a distinct genus, Tatankaceratops could as easily represent a dwarf Triceratops or a Triceratops individual with a developmental disorder

facts.statement: Triceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous period in western North America.
facts.quote: Triceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous of western North America

facts.statement: Fossils of Triceratops have been found in the Evanston, Scollard, Laramie, Lance, Denver, and Hell Creek Formations.
facts.quote: its fossils coming from the Evanston Formation, Scollard Formation, Laramie Formation, Lance Formation, Denver Formation, and Hell Creek Formation

facts.statement: The fossil formations containing Triceratops date back to approximately 66 ± 0.07 million years ago, near the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: These fossil formations date back to the time of the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, which has been dated to 66 ± 0.07 million years ago

facts.statement: Isotopic analysis suggests Triceratops specimens from the Darnell Triceratops Bonebed likely inhabited freshwater floodplains, though they were probably not restricted to a single environment.
facts.quote: Isotopic analysis suggests Triceratops specimens from DTB (Darnell Triceratops Bonebed) could've inhabited freshwater floodplains, although the it likely wasn't restricted to one environment

facts.statement: A mounted Triceratops skeleton was exhibited at the 1900 Paris Exposition, where it was seen by 21,000 visitors in the first two days.
facts.quote: A mounted Triceratops skeleton was exhibited at the 1900 Paris Exposition, possibly the earliest display of the dinosaur, and was seen by 21,000 visitors during the first two days

facts.statement: Triceratops is the official state fossil of South Dakota and the official state dinosaur of Wyoming.
facts.quote: Triceratops is the official state fossil of South Dakota and the official state dinosaur of Wyoming

facts.statement: In 1928, Charles R. Knight painted a mural at the Field Museum of Natural History depicting a confrontation between a Tyrannosaurus and a Triceratops, establishing them as enemies in popular culture.
facts.quote: In 1928, Charles R. Knight painted a mural incorporating a confrontation between a Tyrannosaurus and a Triceratops in the Field Museum of Natural History in Chicago, establishing them as enemies in the popular imagination

facts.statement: Triceratops lived in North America during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago, in the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 68 y 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Triceratops had a large bony frill covering the top and sides of its neck and three horns, along with a large body supported by four sturdy legs.
facts.quote: Poseía una gran gola ósea que le cubría dorsal y lateralmente el cuello y tres cuernos, un cuerpo grande sobre cuatro robustas patas

facts.statement: Triceratops was one of the largest dinosaurs, reaching lengths of up to 8 to 9 meters and weighing between 5 to 9 metric tons.
facts.quote: También fue uno de los más grandes, de hasta 8 a 9 metros de largo y de 5 a 9 toneladas métricas de masa corporal

facts.statement: No complete Triceratops skeleton has been found yet, though the animal is well documented by numerous partial remains collected since the genus was introduced in 1887.
facts.quote: Aún no se ha encontrado un esqueleto completo de Triceratops, aunque la criatura está bien documentada por numerosos restos parciales recogidos desde la introducción del género en 1887

facts.statement: While traditionally viewed as defensive weapons against predators, recent theories suggest the frill and horns were more likely used for sexual courtship and dominance displays.
facts.quote: Aunque se vean tradicionalmente como armas defensivas contra depredadores, las últimas teorías proponen que es más probable que estas características fueran utilizadas durante el cortejo sexual y en exhibiciones de dominancia

facts.statement: Triceratops is traditionally placed in Centrosaurinae but modern cladistic studies show it is a member of Chasmosaurinae, which typically have long frills.
facts.quote: Tradicionalmente se sitúa dentro de los Centrosaurinae, "con volantes cortos", pero los estudios cladísticos modernos muestran que es un miembro de Chasmosaurinae que generalmente tiene "volantes largos"

facts.statement: Two species, Triceratops horridus and Triceratops prorsus, are currently considered valid.
facts.quote: Dos especies, Triceratops horridus y Triceratops prorsus, son actualmente consideradas válidas

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that Torosaurus may represent a fully mature form of Triceratops rather than a separate genus.
facts.quote: Recientes investigaciones parecen apuntar a que el conocido ceratópsido, Torosaurus, representa una forma completamente madura de Triceratops más que un género aparte

facts.statement: Although Triceratops shared territory with the fearsome Tyrannosaurus and was hunted by it, it is unclear whether they fought in the manner often depicted in museum displays or popular images.
facts.quote: Aunque compartiera el territorio con el temible Tyrannosaurus y fuera cazado por él, no está claro si los dos lucharon de la manera representada a menudo en exhibiciones de museo o en imágenes populares

facts.statement: The Triceratops skeleton is notably robust, with both species having a sturdy constitution, strong limbs, short hands with three claws each, and short feet with four claws each.
facts.quote: El esqueleto de Triceratops es notablemente robusto. Ambas especies de Triceratops poseían una constitución robusta, con extremidades fuertes, manos cortas con tres pezuñas cada una y pies cortos con cuatro pezuñas cada uno

facts.statement: The Triceratops spine consisted of 10 neck vertebrae, 10 back vertebrae, 10 sacral vertebrae, and about 45 tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral constaba de 10 vértebras del cuello, 10 de la espalda, 10 sacras y unas 45 de la cola

facts.statement: In Triceratops, the neural spines of the neck have a constant height instead of gradually inclining upwards.
facts.quote: En Triceratops las espinas neurales del cuello tienen una altura constante, en lugar de inclinarse gradualmente hacia arriba

facts.statement: Triceratops skin impressions consist of large hexagonal tubercles 50 to 60 millimeters wide, along with larger tubercles about 100 millimeters wide with conical projections.
facts.quote: Estos consisten en tubérculos hexagonales grandes de entre 50 a 60 milímetros de ancho, junto con tubérculos más grandes de alrededor de 100 milímetros de ancho con proyecciones cónicas

facts.statement: Triceratops horridus, originally named Ceratops, was described by Marsh in 1889 and is the type species.
facts.quote: Triceratops horridus (Marsh, 1889) (originalmente Ceratops) (especie tipo)

facts.statement: Triceratops prorsus was described by Marsh in 1890.
facts.quote: Triceratops prorsus (Marsh, 1890)

facts.statement: To date, only one site in southeastern Montana has yielded multiple Triceratops specimens, consisting of three juveniles.
facts.quote: hasta la fecha solo hay un yacimiento documentado con varios ejemplares de Triceratops: un lugar en el sudeste de Montana con restos de tres jóvenes.

facts.statement: In 2012, a group of three Triceratops of varying sizes, from an adult to a small juvenile, was found near Newcastle, Wyoming.
facts.quote: En 2012, cerca de Newcastle, Wyoming, se encontró un grupo de tres Triceratops en condiciones relativamente completas, cada uno de diferentes tamaños, desde un adulto hasta un pequeño juvenil.

facts.statement: Remains show signs of predation or scavenging by Tyrannosaurus, specifically on the largest specimen, with fractures and puncture wounds on the forelimb bones.
facts.quote: Los restos también muestran signos de depredación o carroña por parte de Tyrannosaurus, particularmente en el espécimen más grande, con los huesos de las extremidades delanteras que muestran roturas y heridas punzantes de los dientes del depredador.

facts.statement: In 2020, Illies and Fowler described fused distal caudal vertebrae in Triceratops.
facts.quote: En 2020, Illies y Fowler describieron las vértebras caudales distales coosificadas de Triceratops.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Bruce Erickson reported that 200 specimens of T. prorsus are known from the Hell Creek Formation in Montana.
facts.quote: Bruce Erickson, un paleontólogo del Museo de Ciencias de Minnesota, ha reportado que se conocen 200 especímenes de T. prorsus en la Formación Hell Creek de Montana.

facts.statement: Triceratops is considered one of the dominant herbivores of its time, living 68 to 65 million years ago in western North America during the late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Debido a que los dientes, fragmentos de los cuernos, de la gola, y otros fragmentos del cráneo de Triceratops son los fósiles más abundantes en la Formación Lance, de finales del Maastrichtiense durante el Cretácico Superior, hace 68 a 65 millones de años en Norteamérica occidental, Triceratops está considerado como uno de los herbívoros dominantes de su tiempo, si no el más dominante.

facts.statement: In 1986, Robert Bakker estimated that Triceratops made up 5/6 of the large dinosaur fauna at the end of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: En 1986, Robert Bakker estimó que componía 5/6 de la fauna de grandes dinosaurios a finales del Cretácico.

facts.statement: Analysis of endocranial anatomy suggests Triceratops had a poor sense of smell compared to other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El análisis de la anatomía endocraneal de Triceratops sugiere que su sentido del olfato era pobre en comparación con el de otros dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Studies suggest Triceratops held its head at about 45 degrees to the ground, a posture that would effectively display its horns and frill while allowing it to graze.
facts.quote: Este mismo estudio también sugiere que Triceratops mantuvo su cabeza a unos 45 grados con respecto del suelo, un ángulo que exhibiría los cuernos y el volante de la manera más efectiva y al mismo tiempo permitiría que el animal aprovechara la comida a través del pastoreo.

facts.statement: A 2022 study by Wiemann and colleagues suggests Triceratops had an ectothermic or gigantothermic metabolism similar to modern reptiles.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2022 realizado por Wiemann y sus colegas de varios géneros de dinosaurios, incluido el Triceratops, sugiere que tenía un metabolismo ectotérmico, de sangre fría, o gigantotérmico, a la par con el de los reptiles modernos.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that such metabolisms may have been common for ornithischian dinosaurs in general, evolving from an endothermic ancestor.
facts.quote: Sugirieron que tales metabolismos pueden haber sido comunes para los dinosaurios ornitisquios en general y que el grupo evolucionó hacia la ectotermia a partir de un antepasado con un metabolismo endotérmico, de sangre caliente.

facts.statement: The jaws ended in a deep, narrow beak thought to be better adapted for stripping and browsing than for biting.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas terminaban en un pico profundo y estrecho, del que se piensa que estaba más adaptado para arrancar y ramonear que para morder.

facts.statement: The large size and number of teeth suggest Triceratops ate large volumes of fibrous plant material, possibly including palms, cycads, or prairie ferns.
facts.quote: El gran tamaño y número de los dientes de un Triceratops sugiere que comían volúmenes grandes de material vegetal fibroso, por lo que se ha sugerido que palmeras y cycas formaban la mayor parte de su dieta, o helechos, que crecerían en praderas.

facts.statement: There is debate over the function of Triceratops' main features, with theories ranging from combat to courtship display, the latter being considered the most probable primary function.
facts.quote: Ha habido mucha especulación sobre las funciones de las características principales de Triceratops. Las dos teorías principales han girado alrededor de uso en combate, o exhibición en el cortejo, con esta última idea considerada como la función primaria más probable.

facts.statement: Early studies proposed by Lull suggested the frill served as an anchor for mastication muscles to increase bite power.
facts.quote: En los primeros estudios sobre el género, Lull propuso que la gola o volante craneal posterior pudiera servir de anclaje a los músculos de la masticación, permitiéndole una mayor potencia muscular.

facts.statement: Later studies failed to find evidence of large muscle attachment areas on the frill bones, contradicting the earlier hypothesis.
facts.quote: Esto fue aceptado por otros autores durante muchos años, pero estudios posteriores no encontraron pruebas de grandes zonas de inserción muscular en los huesos de la gola.

facts.statement: The first extensive ontogenetic study of Triceratops was published in 2006 in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society.
facts.quote: En 2006, se publicó el primer estudio ontogenético extenso de Triceratops en la revista Proceedings of the Royal Society.

facts.statement: Among the 28 skulls studied, the youngest measured only 38 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Con un número total de 28 cráneos estudiados, el más joven medía solo 38 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Multiple ontogenetic trends were discovered, including the reduction of epoccipitals, the development and reorientation of postorbital horns, and the hollowing of the horns.
facts.quote: Se descubrieron múltiples tendencias ontogenéticas, incluida la reducción del tamaño de los epoccipitales, el desarrollo y la reorientación de los cuernos postorbitales y el ahuecamiento de los cuernos.

facts.statement: Large eyes and shortened features suggest that Triceratops parents may have cared for their young.
facts.quote: Los ojos grandes y las características acortadas, un sello de "lindo" en los mamíferos bebé, también sugieren que los padres Triceratops pueden haber cuidado a sus jóvenes.

facts.statement: Triceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Triceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.

facts.statement: A 2026 study used a biomechanical model to suggest that the hunting strategy involving Tyrannosaurus colliding with Triceratops proposed by Krauss & Robinson (2013) was unlikely to be frequently used.
facts.quote: Blanco, Luzardo-Vera & Yorio (2026) use a biomechanical model originally developed for assessment of injury risk of extant leopards while hunting by free-falling from trees to estimate the risk of injury that could be sustained by Tyrannosaurus colliding with Triceratops, and interpret the hunting strategy involving collision with Triceratops proposed by Krauss & Robinson (2013) as unlikely to be frequently used by Tyrannosaurus.
